London Advanced · Journal

London, reported
from the pavement.

Places, walks and details that reward a second look. Written from direct experience, checked against sources and paired with original photography.

By Paolo Pastorino
Latest stories

No artificial publishing quota: only work that earns the reader’s time.

Angel · Markets and independent shops

Camden Passage in Angel: antiques, food and a better reason to linger

This pedestrian lane is not in Camden Town. Come to Angel for the antiques market, then stay for the shopfronts, cafés and a compact piece of Islington street life.

Twickenham · Music and artists

Eel Pie Island: music, makers and how to visit a private Thames island

A footbridge crosses to one of London’s most mythologised islands. Most days it leads to private homes and working boatyards; on Open Studios weekends, another world briefly opens.

24 October 2026Read →
North London · Railway walk

Parkland Walk: the railway that became a forest

Between Finsbury Park and Highgate, trees have colonised a former railway without erasing it. Platforms, bridges and cuttings still dictate the route.

24 October 2026Read →
Across London · Neighbourhood food

Five London food markets beyond Borough: eat locally, explore further

The best market visit is not a race between stalls. Choose the right market for the day, eat something good and use it to understand the neighbourhood around it.

16 October 2026Read →
Across London · Independent browsing

Five unusual London bookshops worth crossing the city for

A shop overflowing onto the pavement, an eighteenth-century frontage, a book barge, poetry on prescription and a former bank make browsing part of the journey.

16 October 2026Read →
Across London · Unexpected views

Five unusual London viewpoints where the ground matters as much as the skyline

A dockland mound, a market clock tower, ancient woodland, a protected sightline and a department-store café show five different ways to read London from above.

16 October 2026Read →
Across London · Community farms

London’s city farms: seven free rural pockets built for their communities

Come for the goats, pigs and skyline views; stay for the training, food growing, volunteering and neighbourhood networks that explain why these farms exist.

12 October 2026Read →
Across London · Community gardens

London’s community gardens: seven small spaces reclaimed by local people

These are not miniature parks. They are pieces of bombsite, railway land, alley and threatened open space made useful through local work and persistence.

12 October 2026Read →
Across London · Victorian cemeteries

London’s Magnificent Seven cemeteries: the six beyond Highgate

Highgate is only one chapter. London’s other six great Victorian cemeteries tell different stories about architecture, migration, reform, wildlife and local memory.

12 October 2026Read →
South-west London · Sacred spaces

Buddhapadipa Temple: how to visit Wimbledon’s Thai sanctuary

Behind a suburban gate in Wimbledon stands Britain’s first purpose-built Thai Buddhist temple: an active monastery where architecture, murals and gardens reward a quiet visit.

2 October 2026Read →
West London · Art and landscape

Chiswick beyond the High Road: Hogarth, Palladio and a house of mosaics

A short Chiswick circuit links three very different ideas of a house: Hogarth’s modest retreat, a Palladian villa in a designed landscape and a home covered in contemporary mosaics.

2 October 2026Read →
South London · Lost architecture

Crystal Palace Park: reconstructing a vanished palace

Dinosaurs, sphinxes, a tiled subway and a vast transmitter look unrelated. Together they reveal the scale and ambition of the Crystal Palace destroyed in 1936.

2 October 2026Read →
North London · Cemetery landscapes

Highgate Cemetery beyond Marx: what East and West reveal

Karl Marx is the famous name, but Highgate is most rewarding when read as two different landscapes: the open East Cemetery and the theatrical, wooded West.

2 October 2026Read →
South London · River route

The Wandle Trail: London’s other river, from mills to the Thames

The Wandle is only about 20 kilometres long, but it compresses an extraordinary amount of London into its course: chalk-stream nature, suburban parks, lost industries and a working river mouth.

City fringe · Dissenting London

Wesley’s Chapel and Bunhill Fields: dissent beside the City

Across one short stretch of City Road, a Methodist chapel, an eighteenth-century house and a burial ground reveal the world of Londoners who worshipped outside the established church.

South-east London · Walking route

Blackheath to Greenwich: the slow way down the hill

Start with village shops, cross the open heath and enter Greenwich Park from above. The famous view comes later; the quieter route towards it is the real pleasure.

City of London · Urban walks

The City of London dragon walk: follow the boundary most people miss

White dragons stand guard where the City begins. Link them together and a familiar business district turns into a walk through boundaries, lost gates and stubborn fragments of old London.

City of London · Free viewpoints

One Leadenhall terrace: London’s best new low-level view?

This is not another race to the top of the skyline. Four floors above Leadenhall Market, the terrace succeeds because the City remains close enough to read.

Clerkenwell · Illustration

Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration: beyond the familiar drawings

London’s new home for illustration uses a beautifully restored industrial site to make the case that drawings are not the supporting act. They are the story.

Leamouth · Industrial London

Trinity Buoy Wharf: London’s lighthouse at the edge of the Thames

A lighthouse that never guided ships to sea, a composition designed to last a thousand years and one of east London’s strangest riverside corners.

Hackney Wick · Museums

V&A East Storehouse: the museum that shows its workings

Half a million objects, open storage and a museum that turns its backstage machinery into part of the visit. The scale is striking; the freedom to follow your own curiosity is the real point.
